guarantees.claim: When rst_ni is low (reset active), msg_allowed is cleared to 0.
When hash_start_or_continue is high (and not in reset), msg_allowed is set to 1.
guarantees.cond: posedge clk_i with hash_start_or_continue == 1 and rst_ni == 1

guarantees.claim: When packer_flush_done is high, hash_start_or_continue is low, and not in reset, msg_allowed is cleared to 0.
guarantees.cond: posedge clk_i with packer_flush_done == 1, hash_start_or_continue == 0, rst_ni == 1

guarantees.claim: If none of rst_ni, hash_start_or_continue, or packer_flush_done conditions are true, msg_allowed retains its previous value.
guarantees.cond: posedge clk_i with rst_ni == 1, hash_start_or_continue == 0, packer_flush_done == 0

assumptions.claim: External logic must not assert both hash_start_or_continue and packer_flush_done in the same clock cycle.
assumptions.cond: Any clock edge where both signals are high
assumptions.risk: msg_allowed will be set to 1, ignoring the packer_flush_done clear, potentially allowing new message data after a flush when it should be blocked.

uncertain_points.claim: The priority of hash_start_or_continue over packer_flush_done may be intentional or a bug. If both can occur together due to timing, the intended behavior needs to be clarified.
uncertain_points.cond: When packer_flush_done coincides with a new hash start request.
uncertain_points.risk: If the intent is to clear msg_allowed on packer_flush_done regardless of hash_start_or_continue, the current logic may leave msg_allowed high, causing a message acceptance control violation.
